outcome: fetal prenatal ultrasound measurements (biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, and their z-scores)
cohort: The study included 46 pregnant women diagnosed with COVID-19 in mid-pregnancy and a control group of 92 pregnant women negative for COVID-19, all recruited between December 2022 and June 2023.
finding: While gestational diabetes differed significantly between groups, fetal growth rate, estimated fetal weight, pregnancy outcomes, and neonatal prognoses did not significantly differ between pregnant women with and without COVID-19 in mid-pregnancy.
gest_age: fetal growth was assessed between the second and third trimesters
